pr_title: Update glamour to version which includes emoji support
pr_body:
This PR updates our version of `glamour` to v0.3.0 which includes my patch for emoji support. It also removes our previous workaround for emoji support in favor of the new `glamour` feature.

Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2352

issue_context.title: Emoji parser does not discriminate
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

After emoji parsing was added (#1816) there are unintended side effects when `:xxx:` substrings are contained within `README`'s.

```sh
$ gh --version
gh version 1.2.0 (2020-10-27)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Type e.g. `gh repo view strongswan/strongswan` and note the German flag in the middle...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1992842/97876465-e29f9900-1ce9-11eb-9831-1a4c69fb573d.png)

from [strongswan/README.md](https://github.com/strongswan/strongswan/blob/master/README.md#revoking-a-certificate):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1992842/97877191-cea86700-1cea-11eb-956d-57458eeeb360.png)
comments: Hi there! Is this issue still open? I might be interested in taking a deeper look at this; does your team have any resources or tips you'd recommend to get started? Thanks!

@divyaramanathan This issue is still open and available to be worked on. We are using https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour to parse our markdown right now, which in turn uses https://github.com/yuin/goldmark. The `goldmark` library already has an emoji extension (https://github.com/yuin/goldmark-emoji) that we should try to use. I think the difficult part is just figuring out how to get that extension working with `glamour`.

@samcoe Hi, I'm working on this issue with @divyaramanathan, and we wanted to confirm the correct behavior for this defect. We've found [this repo](https://github.com/ikatyang/emoji-cheat-sheet) that uses emojis as well as plaintext following the `:word:` format. We think the correct behavior would be to not render emojis in code blocks. This would reflect behavior on the Github website. Are we on the right track with this idea? thanks!

@zaboyle That is correct, we want to keep the same behavior that we see on GitHub which would be not rendering emoji in code blocks. Also, it seems that the `goldmark-emoji` extension I linked above already has the GitHub emoji definitions (https://github.com/yuin/goldmark-emoji/blob/master/definition/github.go) so I would expect that to work as is without having to introduce another library for those definitions.

@samcoe me and @divyaramanathan are currently toying with `goldmark-emoji`. We were able add the dependency and  modify the rendering of the  `:de:` in the `strongswan/strongswan` README
from the original
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33520963/98896735-af8e9f80-2477-11eb-863f-d4ed59aff33a.png)

to
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33520963/98896992-570bd200-2478-11eb-9a58-030ec142f997.png)

We think this is still incorrect because it seems the `goldmark-emoji` parser is still trying to render this `:de:` as an emoji. We're unsure of where to go from here (maybe dig into some of the `glamour` internals?), and would appreciate any advice you may have!

We can make a draft PR with our current changes if you'd like!

Thanks!

Just to add on to what @zaboyle said, `🇩` is the Unicode hex character code for 'd' and then `🇪` is the  Unicode hex character code for 'e'.

I believe we are very close-- do you think this could relate to the type of terminal we're running on?
@zaboyle @divyaramanathan It seems unlikely that it is related to the terminal you are running. I think it would be easiest to open a draft PR so that I can better help with resolving this issue.

I don't have a strong opinion here. I am comfortable leaving it as is, with some incorrect replacements, until the upstream PR gets merged. If more issues get opened regarding this bug or more people chime in saying they are encountering it then we could reevaluate and revert the change then.

I am not sure if this should be mentioned here, but some emojis are not working in Command Prompt.
![gitcli](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55401175/101509035-56def380-399e-11eb-923c-8f9541934c0a.PNG)
The Tick emoji(✓) to be precise.

A quick update here. The upstream PR https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/pull/92 was merged in 🎉! Now we just need to wait for the next release of `glamour`. 

@garvit-joshi That is interesting. This issue is specifically for emoji rendering in our markdown renderer, where as it appears you are having rendering issues in our survey code. I think it would be best to keep these separate, so if you wouldn't mind opening a new issue that would be much appreciated.

review_comments: This change disables emoji support in non-Markdown documents, but I'm okay with that.
